title: Construct an equilateral triangle on an arbitrary nondegenerate segment
model: real-coordinate Euclidean plane; analytic construction with source-property certificates

variables.domain: arbitrary points in the Euclidean plane

required_conclusions.statement: For every A and B satisfying H1, there exists a point C in the plane.
The lengths of AB, AC and BC are equal.
A, B and C are noncollinear and form a nondegenerate triangle.
C lies on the circle with center A and radius AB.
C lies on the circle with center B and radius BA.

construction_requirements: Define and identify the two prescribed circles.
Construct a witness and prove its specified properties.
Explain the correspondence between the analytic proof and the source circle-intersection construction.
permitted_presentations: Squared distance may be used if its correspondence to equal lengths is justified.
A witness on either side of AB is allowed; uniqueness is not required.
forbidden_weakening: Proving only a fixed numerical segment.
Assuming a circle intersection exists without proof.
Adding premises absent from the source to avoid the target.

source.delivery_requirement: Package the same bounded source text and needed definition texts for both languages. This experiment provides no images.

success_policy.accuracy_definition: machine-verified propositions divided by registered propositions
